newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Investors pick and choose among HK's red chips.
newsitem.headline: Investors pick and choose among HK's red chips.

text.p: Red chip China plays listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange have blossomed over the past year, but analysts and institutional investors are still picking just a handfull.
"I have only six on my list," said the research head of a European fund management house that claims to be overweight in red chips.
Red chips -- Hong Kong-incorporated and listed companies with a China-based parent -- have been the most active new investment sector in the Hong Kong market in 1996 and 1997.
Building a large portfolio of investment-quality red chips is still difficult due to the highly speculative nature of their growth potential, analysts said.
Few have a long track record as a listed company, but are seen as the best means to tap China's economic growth potential.
Many China analysts have put together similar portfolios out of the 40 or so red chips in the Hong Kong market.
Top picks include conglomerates China Resources Enterprise Ltd, China Merchants Hai Hong Holdings Ltd, Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd and CITIC Pacific Ltd, analysts said.
The second tier includes Silver Grant International Industries Ltd, COSCO Pacific Ltd, Guangzhou Investment Co Ltd, Ng Fung Hong Ltd, Guangnan (Holdings) Ltd and Guangdong Investment Ltd.
At a distant third are Founder (Hong Kong) Ltd, Min Xin Holdings Ltd and China Everbright IHD-Pacific Ltd.
Many other red-chip issues are considered too speculative or too high-risk for institutional investment.
The market has bid up the top tier to very lofty levels in the past year.
At Monday's closing prices, China Resources has risen 361 percent, Shanghai Industrial 354 percent, CITIC Pacific 55 percent and China Merchants Hai Hong 285 percent.
Despite these hefty gains, they remain on the buy list, analysts said.

The first-tier red chips have a well-established parent in China that controls a rich portfolio of assets and profitable operations. The attraction is the possibility the parent will inject some of the assets into the Hong Kong-listed company.
Shanghai Industrial, for example, ranks at the top of Merrill Lynch's Red Chip Scorecard because it has the most asset-rich parent, said John Pinkel, head of China research.
Not yet in the premier league, Silver Grant is one share that is also gathering increasing attention, analysts said.
"It has good potential," said Richard Lo, China research chief at BZW Securities Asia. "It is in the early growth stage and management is open-minded."

Silver Grant, like Guangdong Investment, China Resources Enterprises and others, has great earnings upside due to the potential windfall from the spin-off of some of its divisions into separate listings, said Jeannie Chung, China research analyst at Asia Equity Ltd.

"Silver Grant has been a massive outperformer," Chung said. "There should still be considerable share price upside...given the potential spin-off of its 40-percent owned China Infrastructure Investment Corp in the fourth quarter of this year or in 1998."
Others prefer specialised red chips, such as Ng Fung Hong, Guangnan and COSCO Pacific, which invest in specified areas.

"We are confident that whatever assets they acquire...they will manage the new acquisitions better," said Lawrence Ang, head of China research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "I think the focus will shift back to specialised red chips."
